Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

responsible adjective

reliable, conscientious

also conscientious, dutiful, a responsible person, reliable (of a person)

classical

Cic. Cael. 73: omnis officiī dīligentissimus (Lewis & Short, s.v. dīligō)
Cic. Lael. 62: in rēbus omnibus

dīligēns, dīligentis

adjective, third declension; with in + ablative or the genitive · Declension on Wiktionary

careful, conscientious, attentive

The opposite of neglegēns: someone who takes care over what is entrusted to him.

Other words

  • officiī memor — mindful of one’s duty

    phrase: memor + genitive · also used · classical · Sen. Ben. 4.20 (M-O s.v. responsible)

    Morgan–Owens’s rendering of “having a sense of responsibility”.

Examples

  • omnis officiī dīligentissimus

    most conscientious in every dutyCic. Cael. 73 (Lewis & Short)

  • Fīlius tuus dīligentissimus est.

    Your son is very responsible.composed

See also responsible, in charge, sense.

SourcesLewis & Short: diligo · Lewis & Short: memor · Lewis & Short: officium

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. responsible.

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
